name: Pleistocene Canis Proximal Phalanx UW57662
description: This 3D model represents UW-57662, a proximal phalanx (the first bone of a toe) from the genus Canis, discovered in 2022 at Natural Trap Cave (on Bureau of Land Managment land, and curated at the University of Wyoming).  The bone dates to the Pleistocene and may belong to either a wolf or a coyote—distinguishing between the two is challenging because research from Natural Trap Cave has shown that Ice Age coyotes were significantly larger than their modern counterparts, creating strong overlap with wolves. Natural Trap Cave itself is an 85-foot limestone pit near the Bighorn Mountains that acted as a natural animal trap for tens of thousands of years, preserving an exceptional record of Ice Age fauna. This specimen is part of that rich archive of Wyoming’s Pleistocene predators.
